samples.summary: The new "wait for the stylesheet before asking the Font Loading API" gate in applySlideFontFamily has no test at all
samples.evidence: This delta changes applySlideFontFamily from `document.fonts.load(...)` to `ensureFontLink(family).then(() => document.fonts.load(...))`, and the docblock calls the wait "LOAD-BEARING" (a subset face would otherwise answer the load and be what the single dirty-gated repaint paints). Nothing exercises it: grep for `applySlideFontFamily`/`apply-font-family` across the repo returns only the two call sites (slides `text-edit-section.tsx`, `mobile-toolbar.tsx`), docs and task notes — no test file. `packages/frontend/tests/app/slides/toolbar/text-edit-section.test.ts` only supplies a no-op `markDirty()` editor stub and never touches `document.fonts`, and `tests/app/slides/themed-font-picker.test.ts`/`tests/app/slides/*` contain no `document.fonts` reference. So the ordering (link settled -> fonts.load -> markDirty+render) could regress to the pre-delta behaviour with every suite still green.

samples.summary: The release-BEFORE-onChange call in applyPick is untested; every new test only covers the unmount-cleanup path
samples.evidence: `applyPick` adds `releasePreviewFontLinks()` ahead of `onChange`, justified in-comment as covering "the window between the list unmounting and its effect cleanup firing" so the caller's `document.fonts.check()/load()` cannot be answered by a subset. The two new tests cover the other path only: "closing the menu releases the row subsets" (font-family-picker.test.ts:445) dismisses with Esc and never picks, and "closing the dialog releases the row subsets" (more-fonts-dialog.test.ts:183) re-renders with open=false. The pre-existing pick test "selecting a previewed-only family still loads the full family" (font-family-picker.test.ts:405) only asserts a full `<link>` exists after the click — it never asserts `previewLinks()` is empty at the moment `onChange` runs, and would pass identically with line 198 deleted (the unmount cleanup removes the subset anyway, just later). No test captures the ordering, e.g. an `onChange` spy recording `previewLinks().length`.

samples.summary: The deliberate "keyed on listEl/scrollEl alone" dependency choice is untested — nothing pins that subsets survive while the list is still open
samples.evidence: Both new effects carry an explicit design claim that the deps must NOT include the observer effect's deps (`recents`, `fullByFamily`, `fullSettled` in the picker; `results` in the dialog), because releasing on those re-runs "would drop faces the open list still paints". No test drives such a re-run (e.g. resolve the full-catalog load so `fullSettled`/`fullByFamily` change, or type in the dialog's search box to re-filter) and then asserts the previously injected subset link is still connected. Adding `results`/`recents` to the dep arrays would regress the very bug the comment names while both new release tests stay green.
searchedFor: read font-family-picker.tsx around the new effect and observer effect deps
full read of both new test files for any re-filter/search-driven assertion on previewLinks

verdict.reason: applySlideFontFamily (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/apply-font-family.ts:30-47) gates document.fonts.load behind ensureFontLink's settled promise before the single dirty-gated repaint, and the docblock (lines 23-28) calls that wait load-bearing. No test in the repository imports or exercises the helper: repo-wide greps for `applySlideFontFamily` and `apply-font-family` return only the two call sites plus docs; the colocated src test tree (src/app/slides/toolbar/index.test.tsx, theme-fonts.test.ts) has no font-family-apply coverage; tests/app/slides/toolbar/text-edit-section.test.ts only smoke-imports the component (line 220-225) with a no-op markDirty/render stub and no spies; mobile-text-toggles.test.ts never touches the family picker. All of these stay green if the helper regressed to an ungated document.fonts.load, so the ordering (link settled -> fonts.load -> markDirty+render) has no meaningful coverage.
